title: The Snail Who Beat the Heatwave 🐌☀️
yt_title: The Snail Who Beat the Heatwave 🐌☀️
yt_description:
Rocco the rabbit bet that Shelly the snail couldn't last a heatwave in the garden. Then the squirrel found a tiny door on her shell. 🐌🚪
Snails really do this: in dry heat they seal their shell with a thin door of dried slime (an epiphragm), slow their body right down and wait for rain, sometimes for months. (The story is fiction; the snail behaviour is real.)

Sources: Wikipedia "Epiphragm" and "Aestivation".

script: The garden is melting. And Shelly the snail just bet she can outlast the fastest rabbit in town. Rocco the rabbit cannot stop laughing. You? You're a slow little jelly in a teacup! The squirrel reads the rules. Nobody goes to the pond. Last one still in the garden wins. Day one. Rocco licks the dew, digs a cool hole, and flexes for the crowd. Shelly? She climbs a fence post. Right into the full sun. And stops. Day three. The puddles are gone. The grass is crunchy. Rocco's ears start to droop. Shelly hasn't moved at all. Rocco pokes her shell. She's cooked. Totally cooked! Day five. Rocco is panting like a broken fan, dreaming about ice cream carrots. The squirrel knocks on Shelly's shell. Tap, tap. There's a door. A thin white door, sealed shut. And from inside, a sleepy little voice says: wake me when it rains. Day seven. Rocco snaps. He sprints to the pond. Splash! Disqualified. That night, the rain comes. The tiny door pops open, and Shelly stretches out, fresh as a lettuce. Snails really do this: in dry heat, they seal their shell with a door of dried slime, slow their body right down, and wait for rain for months. Next summer, Rocco wants a rematch. Shelly is already on her fence post.
